items.question: What is the minimum wage for private sector employees in Sri Lanka?
items.notes: Out-of-corpus: minimum wage is governed by Wages Board Ordinance and subsidiary legislation, not the Constitution.

items.question: What is the personal income tax rate for individuals earning over Rs. 3 million per year in Sri Lanka?
items.notes: Out-of-corpus: income tax rates are set by the Inland Revenue Act, not the Constitution.

items.question: What notice period must an employer give before dismissing an employee in Sri Lanka?
items.notes: Out-of-corpus: dismissal notice periods are governed by the Termination of Employment of Workmen Act.

items.question: What is the process and fee for registering a private limited company in Sri Lanka?
items.notes: Out-of-corpus: company registration is governed by the Companies Act No. 7 of 2007.

items.question: What are the penalties for copyright infringement in Sri Lanka?
items.notes: Out-of-corpus: copyright penalties are governed by the Intellectual Property Act No. 36 of 2003.

items.question: What are the conditions for granting bail to a person accused of theft in Sri Lanka?
items.notes: Out-of-corpus: bail conditions are governed by the Code of Criminal Procedure Act and Bail Act.

items.question: What are the mandatory minimum penalties for drug trafficking offences in Sri Lanka?
items.notes: Out-of-corpus: drug trafficking penalties are governed by the Poisons, Opium and Dangerous Drugs Ordinance and Drugs Act.

items.question: How does a foreign national apply for a tourist visa to visit Sri Lanka?
items.notes: Out-of-corpus: visa procedures are governed by the Immigrants and Emigrants Act, not the Constitution.

items.question: On what grounds can a person file for divorce in Sri Lanka?
items.notes: Out-of-corpus: divorce grounds are governed by the Matrimonial Causes Ordinance and personal laws.

items.question: What fines can be imposed on a company for selling defective goods to consumers in Sri Lanka?
items.notes: Out-of-corpus: consumer protection fines are governed by the Consumer Affairs Authority Act.

items.question: What are the regulations governing the maximum interest rate that banks can charge on personal loans in Sri Lanka?
items.notes: Out-of-corpus: interest rate regulations are governed by the Central Bank of Sri Lanka Act and Monetary Board directions.

items.question: What environmental impact assessment is required before constructing a hotel near a coastal area in Sri Lanka?
items.notes: Out-of-corpus: environmental impact assessments are governed by the National Environmental Act No. 47 of 1980.

items.question: What are the formal requirements for a valid will under Sri Lankan law?
items.notes: Out-of-corpus: will requirements are governed by the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance and Wills Ordinance.

items.question: What are the speed limits on expressways in Sri Lanka and what penalty applies for exceeding them?
items.notes: Out-of-corpus: speed limits and traffic penalties are governed by the Motor Traffic Act.

items.question: What licence is required to operate a restaurant in Colombo and how is it obtained?
items.notes: Out-of-corpus: restaurant licensing is governed by local authority by-laws and the Food Act.

items.question: What is the minimum age required to vote in a Sri Lankan general election?
items.notes: In-corpus control: Article 89 of the Constitution specifies voting qualifications including age 18.

items.question: What are the functions and powers of the Attorney General of Sri Lanka?
items.notes: In-corpus control: Article 61E of the Constitution sets out the Attorney General's functions.

items.question: What is the term of office of the President of Sri Lanka?
items.notes: In-corpus control: Article 30 of the Constitution specifies the presidential term of office.

items.question: Under what circumstances can a state of emergency be proclaimed in Sri Lanka?
items.notes: In-corpus control: Article 155 of the Constitution governs emergency proclamations.

items.question: How is the Cabinet of Ministers of Sri Lanka constituted and who appoints Ministers?
items.notes: In-corpus control: Article 44 of the Constitution governs the Cabinet of Ministers.
